summary: Defines a new sub-option for the DHCP Relay Agent Information option that identifies the device class in DOCSIS cable networks. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3256 adds a DHCP relay sub-option for the device class of a DOCSIS cable modem. The relay passes the class to the DHCP server, which may use it when choosing configuration for the modem.

subtitle: A DHCP relay sub-option that carries a DOCSIS cable modem's device class.

tldr.problem: A DHCP server may need trusted information about a cable modem's device class to choose configuration policies.
tldr.mechanism: The modem signals a 32-bit device-class value through DOCSIS, and the relay agent forwards that value unchanged to the DHCP server.
tldr.outcome: The server can use the class for policy decisions, while the RFC relies on trust between modem, relay, and server rather than defining cryptographic authentication.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 3256's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines a DHCP Relay Agent Information sub-option for DOCSIS device class.

sections.title: Why the DHCP Server Needs Device Class
sections.content:
The RFC defines a relay-agent sub-option for DOCSIS cable modems. It carries the device class that the modem signals to the relay, so the DHCP server can make a policy decision based on that information.

The memo focuses on CPE Controlled Cable Modems, where firmware controls DOCSIS signaling while an attached computer handles other protocol activities. It says the relay-agent sub-option is preferred over a new DHCP option for this purpose.
sections.plainLanguage: A cable modem can tell the relay what device class it belongs to. The relay forwards that information so the DHCP server can choose a policy.

sections.title: The 32-Bit Device-Class Field
sections.content:
The sub-option carries a 32-bit DOCSIS device-class field. Bit 0 identifies a CPE Controlled Cable Modem when set to 1; bits 1 through 31 are reserved and set to zero.

The sub-option code is 4 and its data length is 4 octets. The relay agent must pass the device-class value unchanged to the DHCP server.
sections.plainLanguage: The field has one defined bit for the CPE Controlled Cable Modem class. The relay must carry the field to the server without changing it.

sections.title: The Trust Assumptions
sections.content:
The operation assumes a trusted relationship between the DHCP relay agent and server, and between the cable modem and relay through DOCSIS signaling. The RFC assumes the modem firmware is trustworthy for the signaling information.

It does not specify cryptographic or other techniques to authenticate the device class. The server's policy decision therefore depends on the trust assumptions described in the document.
sections.plainLanguage: The server trusts that the relay and modem report the class correctly. This RFC does not define a way to verify that report cryptographically.
